name: Koenigsegg CC8S
hook: Only six were built, and Guinness certified the supercharged V8 behind the seats as the most powerful engine ever put in a production car.
story: Picture a five-year-old in Sweden watching a stop-motion film with his father. A bicycle repairman in a tiny village builds a racing car in his shed, and wins with it. The boy was Christian von Koenigsegg. He never let the idea go. At twenty-two he started sketching his own supercar. That was 1994. By 1996 a prototype was being tested on Swedish tracks by real racing drivers, and in 1997 it stood in the sun at the Cannes film festival. Then came years with nothing anyone could buy. This is the car that finally arrived. Six CC8S were built, and the first was handed over at the Geneva show in March 2003. Behind the seats sat a supercharged 4.7-litre V8 making 655 hp. No production car had ever had more. A film, a shed, and a world record.
description: The CC8S was Koenigsegg's first production car and the first supercar Sweden had made. The name is short for Competition Coupe, V8, Supercharged. Body and chassis are carbon fibre, the doors swing up and out on a hinge the company designed itself, and the roof panel lifts off and stows under the front lid. Six were built in 2002 and 2003, largely by hand, in a small workshop in southern Sweden. Every Koenigsegg since descends from it.
